summary: Adversarial verification of a Boundary Remediation Campaign dev branch before integration

blockers.description: REGRESSION + BASH DIVERGENCE (psh/interactive/history_manager.py#_pending_entries). The new pending multiset VIEW resolves owed entries against state.history by TEXT, so a surviving entry with the same text satisfies the pending count of an entry that was deleted. Result: a `history -d`'d command is resurrected into $HISTFILE as a DUPLICATE line — exactly the exit criterion's 'without duplicate file lines' clause, and the base was CORRECT here. It also falsifies three claims the branch ships: the class docstring ('an entry that leaves state.history by ANY route ... thereby leaves pending, so nothing is ever resurrected into the file after it is gone from memory'), the identical sentence added to psh/interactive/CLAUDE.md, and delete_entry's docstring ('a deleted command is never written to the file afterwards'). The pin that NAMES the property — tests/unit/interactive/test_history_state_machine_4b3.py::TestPendingMultisetSemantics::test_a_read_copy_does_not_make_a_deleted_typed_copy_pending, docstring 'the count — not merely the membership — is what is preserved' — has a body that only does seed_file + load_from_file + assert pending == []; it never types and never deletes, so it cannot see the case its name asserts (NAME-VS-BODY). Same mechanism also defeats the pinned 'psh does not leak' claim: `-r otherfile` line 'secret_from_other', user types the same text, `history -d` the typed copy -> tip writes the FOREIGN line into $HISTFILE.
blockers.evidence: REPLAYED, both directions. (1) Unit, own detached worktrees /tmp/remv-t1-{base,tip}-79840, discriminator printed: seed $HISTFILE=['same']; load_from_file(); add_to_history('same'); delete_entry(2,2); save_to_file() -> base bd13b303 FILE=['same'] | tip bc280e8f FILE=['same','same']. Second shape seed=['a'], typed ['a','b'], delete_entry(2,2) -> base FILE=['a','b'] | tip FILE=['a','a','b']. Control (no delete) identical in both. (2) End-to-end piped `--norc -i`, HISTIGNORE='history*:exit', script 'true same\nhistory -d 2\nexit', HISTFILE seeded 'true same': bash 5.2.26 (/opt/homebrew/bin/bash) -> ['true same']; psh@base bd13b303 -> ['true same']; psh@tip bc280e8f -> ['true same','true same']. (3) Leak shape at tip: memory=['secret_from_other'] (the loaded/foreign copy), HISTFILE=['secret_from_other'] written by save. Probes: /tmp/remv-t1-probe_dupview.py, /tmp/remv-t1-e2e_dupview.py, /tmp/remv-t1-probe_leak.py

blockers.description: FALSE BASH CLAIM + SILENTLY DROPPED DIAGNOSTIC (psh/builtins/shell_state.py#_dispatch_options). The rewritten dispatcher returns bare `1` for two-of-`-anrw` under the shipped comment "Combining two of `-a/-n/-r/-w` is an error in bash: rc 1, no message." Live bash 5.2.26 DOES print a message: `bash: history: cannot use more than one of -anrw`. The base also printed a diagnostic. The tip prints NOTHING on any channel, so `history -wa` now fails completely silently — a diagnostic regression that moves psh AWAY from bash, in the one direction the campaign's error-prefix work protects. It is unpinned: the only cell covering these spellings, tests/conformance/bash/test_history_state_machine_conformance.py::TestClusteredFlagsRider::test_cluster_exit_status_matches_bash ('-an','-rw','-nr'), compares EXIT STATUS ONLY (`self._rc` discards stderr into $OTHER/e and never asserts on it), so a module whose class docstring claims bash parity certifies parity it did not measure.
blockers.evidence: REPLAYED across four spellings, piped `--norc -i`, rc captured immediately after the builtin. `history -wa`: bash rc=1 stderr=['bash: history: cannot use more than one of -anrw']; base bd13b303 rc=2 stderr=['psh: history: -wa: invalid option','psh: history: usage: ...']; tip bc280e8f rc=1 stderr=[]. Identical split for `-an`, `-rw`, `-nr`, and `-cwa` (bash rc=1 + message; tip rc=1 + silence). Probe: /tmp/remv-t1-rows3.py

blockers.description: Undeclared, unpinned behavior divergence vs bash 5.2.26 in the rider's cluster dispatch, in a DESTRUCTIVE direction. bash runs AT MOST ONE action per history invocation: when -c or -d is present, the file ops (-a/-n/-r/-w) are suppressed. psh at tip (_dispatch_options in psh/builtins/shell_state.py) applies -c/-d and then STILL runs the file op. Reproduced divergences at tip bc280e8f (piped --norc -i, scrubbed HIST*/PROMPT*, scratch HISTFILE, oracle /opt/homebrew/bin/bash 5.2.26): (a) 'history -cw' with seeded default HISTFILE: bash rc 0, file UNTOUCHED ['S1','S2'] (verified with unset-HISTFILE-before-exit so no exit-save pollution, plus a control showing separate '-c; -w' DOES truncate — instrument validated); psh rc 0, file TRUNCATED to empty. (b) 'history -wd 1' (seed S1, typed keep): bash file ['S1']; psh file ['true keep'] — the seeded line is destroyed. (c) 'history -ad 3' with 3 typed pending: bash file [] (-a never runs); psh file ['true t1','true t2']. (d) 'history -cn': bash MEM=[] (-n never runs); psh MEM=['EXT']. All four were REJECTED rc 2 at base, so this is new behavior introduced by this branch, sanctioned only as 'with its own probed bash semantics' (R1(a)) — and the probed semantics are wrong: SLOT-LEDGER §1.11 claims '-cw/-ca/-cd 1 → rc 0, both ops performed' (FALSE — bash performs only the clear), the _dispatch_options docstring presents 'then the single file operation' as 'Probed against bash 5.2.26', and test_d_takes_the_next_word_when_the_cluster_ends's docstring claims '-ad 1 IS -a plus -d 1, so both run' (FALSE for bash). Root cause is the R2-F1 instrument-mirror failure again: the a7_order.txt -cw cell used a NAMED file created empty, so 'clear-then-write' and '-w never ran' were indistinguishable, and the base psh columns matched vacuously because base rejected all clusters. Related same-family fact: bash 'history -an' fails LOUDLY ('history: cannot use more than one of -anrw') while the docstring claims 'rc 1, no message' and psh fails silently. None of these divergences is in the b1-b5 declared-deviation register, none is pinned (the -cw/-ca/-cd/-an pins assert rc only), and 'anything ELSE shell-observable that moves is a STOP' per the brief.

blockers.description: The completion report's claim 'Six declared deviations …, each both-sides pinned' (also SLOT-LEDGER §3.6 context) is FALSE for b4. b4 = 'named-file read vs the DEFAULT cursor — bash has one global counter, corrupted by a named read'. The bash-side CLAIM is true — I reproduced it independently (seed [D1,D2,D3], 'history -r X' (1 line), external append D4, 'history -n': bash MEM=[D1,D2,D3,X1,D2,D3,D4] — D2,D3 re-read because the named read set the global counter to 1; psh MEM=[D1,D2,D3,X1,D4]) — so this is a one-cell fix, but a stated register commitment was not delivered, which is bounce-grade per banked 4B.2 lesson 10 (a silently-dropped commitment is bounce-grade even when the measurement behind it turns out fine).

It also falsifies three claims the branch ships: the class docstring ('an entry that leaves state.history by ANY route ... thereby leaves pending, so nothing is ever resurrected into the file after it is gone from memory'), the identical sentence added to psh/interactive/CLAUDE.md, and delete_entry's docstring ('a deleted command is never written to the file afterwards'). The pin that NAMES the property — tests/unit/interactive/test_history_state_machine_4b3.py::TestPendingMultisetSemantics::test_a_read_copy_does_not_make_a_deleted_typed_copy_pending, docstring 'the count — not merely the membership — is what is preserved' — has a body that only does seed_file + load_from_file + assert pending == []; it never types and never deletes, so it cannot see the case its name asserts (NAME-VS-BODY). Same mechanism also defeats the pinned 'psh does not leak' claim: `-r otherfile` line 'secret_from_other', user types the same text, `history -d` the typed copy -> tip writes the FOREIGN line into $HISTFILE.

(c) 'history -ad 3' with 3 typed pending: bash file [] (-a never runs); psh file ['true t1','true t2']. (d) 'history -cn': bash MEM=[] (-n never runs); psh MEM=['EXT'].
